Priya (sec): Heads up — Legal flagged a retention exception. Customer SAR needs evidence going back ~3 years and some of the records are in archived snapshots encrypted under our rotation policy. Who owns the KMS/decrypt path for those archives?
Tom (infra): Which storage are we talking about? DB backups or object snapshots?
Priya (sec): s3://redwood-archive/customer-exports/2019-2022. Encrypted with CMK `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ks/cryptoKeys/redwood-archive-key` and we rotated key material last month. Legal needs: 1) scoped access so they can validate items, 2) immutable audit proof of any decrypts, 3) avoid long-lived permission changes.
Elliot (sre): We should avoid long-lived perms. Proposal: create a time-bound service account with JIT role scoped to that bucket + require manual approval for the operation. Run decrypt/redact from a restricted jumpbox and write an artifact receipt.
Sasha (legal): We don't need full plaintext for everything — metadata + redacted excerpts would suffice for the DSAR validation in many cases. Can platform produce a redacted snapshot first?
Jing (platform): We have a redact-export pipeline that streams objects through the PII filter, but it still needs to decrypt the object before redaction. Two options: (a) platform performs decryption using a temporary KMS grant for the SA, or (b) create a one-off re-encrypted copy under a key that Legal can access. Both require coordination with KMS.
Priya (sec): @matt-kms any concerns with issuing temporary grants for decryption and how we capture an immutable audit trail? We need to prove: what was decrypted, who triggered it, and that Legal approved.
matt-kms: Temporary grants are ok. KMS audit logs show grant creation and usage. Note: since the CMK rotated recently, decrypting some ciphertext may require access to older key versions — we have the versions but need to ensure the decrypt path is available. Strongly recommend: use a short-lived grant + write a signed receipt file to an audit-bucket as part of the flow.
Elliot (sre): I'll implement an "unlock" job. Plan: 1) create scoped service account SA: redwood-ephemeral-unlock@ 2) request a KMS grant scoped to that SA for a 4-hour window 3) run redact-export in isolated VPC 4) write signed receipt to s3://redwood-audit/legal-snapshots/1777777777/receipt.json (receipt includes sha256 of objects, s3 version ids, serviceAccount, operator, and UTC timestamps).
Sasha (legal): We also need the RBAC approval chain recorded. Can the approval ticket ID be embedded in the receipt so we have a single artefact linking approval -> operation -> receipt?
Jing (platform): Yes, we can include an approvals field in the receipt and call approvals.redwood.com webhook before the unlock job runs. Need approvals ticket ID passed to the job.
Tom (infra): Who signs off as approver? Product + Legal? @Derek-product please confirm.
Derek-product: I approve for this customer. Ensure data minimization: only extract documents that match DSAR scope (fields + date range). No bulk exports.
Priya (sec): Great. Action items: create JIRA with DSAR scope and attach customer identifiers; @Elliot to build unlock job + receipt; @matt-kms to document grant steps and window; @Jing to adapt redaction pipeline to accept temporary grants + embed approval ID in receipt; @Derek-product to sign approval in portal. ETA: EOD tomorrow for initial run.
Elliot (sre): I'll start now, aiming for EOD. Quick Q: do we want receipts signed with our HSM key or just KMS-signed metadata? I prefer we sign with HSM to avoid later tampering.
matt-kms: KMS can produce an attestation of decryption events in audit logs; for stronger non-repudiation we can sign the receipt blob with our HSM key (recommended). Also: set KMS audit log retention to 2 years for this window.
audit-bot: Suggestion: create a dedicated audit-only role 'legal-audit-viewer' instead of granting Legal direct read to the archive bucket. We'll populate ACLs for the JIT SA during the grant window and remove them immediately after.
Sasha (legal): Thanks, team. Please keep me in the loop on blockers. If the redaction pipeline can't satisfy the DSAR, we'll escalate to a full decrypt request but that will need an explicit high-risk sign-off.
Priya (sec): I'll open the JIRA now and add the DSAR scope + contact info. I'll also add the ticket ID to the approvals portal. Ping me if you need the customer sample to test redaction.
Tom (infra): One more note — ensure we record S3 object version IDs in the receipt so deletion proof is verifiable later.
Elliot (sre): Will do. Receipt will include object keys + versionId + sha256 + operator email.
Priya (sec): Perfect. Thanks everyone. If anything blocks the grant or decrypt path, call it out in this thread.
